title: Grain Boundary Failure and Strengthening in Entropy Stabilized (MoNbTaVW)C4 Ceramic
content: Development of new materials based on the high entropy stabilization paradigm have resulted in new high strength and high temperature resistance materials, often with additional favorable properties of thermal shock resistance and low reactivity [1]. The configurational entropy of a multicomponent, solid solution system is stable at roughly equimolar composition. Entropy stabilized ceramics have demonstrated exceptional stability and resistance [2,3]. Here we investigate (MoNbTaVW)C5 produced using two different sintering protocols, designated “Molly3” and “Molly8”. The Molly8 sintering protocol included an additional step to remove surface oxides from the constituent grains before sintering at 1900 °C. Flexural strength tests showed demonstrated a significant difference between the two samples, with Molly 8 at 360 MPa and Molly3 at 270 MPa.
